2. Civil Revision No. 1092 of 1993, at the instance of the petitioner Mst. Saleha Khatun, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.7.92 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 226 of 1984 allowing the appeal and setting aside those dated 31.5.1984 of the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet decreeing Title Suit No. 24 of 1982 setting declaration that the plaintiff's marriage with the defendant has been dissolved and does not subsist. 

 3. Civil Revision No. 1093 of 1993, at the instance of the petitioner, Mst. Saleha Khatun is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.7.1992 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 227 of 1984 allowing the appeal and setting aside those dated 31.5.1984 of the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet dismissing the Title Suit No. 35 of 1983 for restitution of conjugal rights. 

 9. Both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence in the above mentioned suits and the trial court considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on record decreed the Title Suit No. 24 of 1982 in favour of the plaintiff, Mst. Saleha Khatun declaring that her marriage with the defendant Md. Saleh Ahmed Stands dissolved and no longer subsists and by the same judgment and decree the trial court dismissed the Title Suit No. 35 of 1983 for restitution of conjugal rights filed by the husband Md. Saleh Ahmed. 

 10. Being aggrieved by those judgment and decrees the husband, Md. Saleh Ahmed preferred appeals before the District Judge, Sylhet being Title Appeal No. 226 of 1984 and 227 of 1984 which were subsequently, on transfer, disposed of by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet allowing both the appeals and reversing those of the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet passed in Title Suit Nos. 24 of 1982 and 35 of 1983. 

 11. Being aggrieved by those judgment and decrees Mst. Saleha Khatun has preferred these revisional applications and obtained the present Rules. 

 12. Heard Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Sarder Abul Hossain and Ms. Bilkis Jahan, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner. None appears for the opposite party. Perused the revisional applications, the impugned judgment and decrees, the relevant papers filed along with the revisional applications and the Lower Court Records. 

 13. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the marriage between the petitioner and the opposite party was duly registered and in the kabinnama the husband delegated the power to the wife, the petitioner to repudiate the marriage in the event of happening of any of the contingencies mentioned therein. Non-payment of prompt dower on demand and non-maintenance are two of the several contingencies mentioned in the said clause and since the husband-opposite party failed to pay the prompt dower to the plaintiff on demand it was a valid ground to repudiate her marriage with the opposite party exercising her power to repudiate the marriage delegated to her by her husband, the opposite party an accordingly the petitioner divorced the opposite party by giving notice to the local Union Parishad in compliance with the provisions of section 8 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial court considering these facts passed the impugned judgment and decrees in favour of the petitioner declaring dissolution of her marriage with the opposite party but the appellate court below by misappreciating the facts, circumstances and evidence on record allowed the appeals as above reversing the judgment and decrees passed by the trial court directing restitution of conjugal rights of the petitioner and the opposite party and as such the impugned judgment and decrees are not sustainable in the eye of law. 

 19. It appears that the appellate court below inspire of having found the defendant-opposite party to have not paid the prompt dower to the plaintiff-petitioner on demand reversed the judgment and decrees passed by the trial court in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner directing the defendant-opposite party to pay the prompt dower money to the plaintiff (wife) within a specified time and restoring the conjugal rights of the parties. But law does not empower the court to pass an order directing the husband to pay the prompt dower to his wife within such a specified period of time when the husband himself already violated the essential condition of the Muslim marriage by not giving the prompt dower to his wife on demand. 

 21. However, it is neither desirable nor expected that the court should pass a decree of restitution of conjugal rights where, the relationship of adjustment between the husband and wife is lost or it is otherwise inequitable, impractical or impossible to implement. 

 22. In the instant case when the husband-defendant-opposite party has failed to pay the prompt dower to the wife, plaintiff-petitioner on demand and failed to discharge his marital obligations towards his wife and thereby, since the relationship between the husband and wife reached to a strained and intolerable position the appellate court below should have considered those aspects of the matter. It is found that the court of appeal below erred grievously in law in not considering those cardinal aspects of the matter and thereby it has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decrees passed by the court of appeal below are not sustainable in the eye of law. 

 24. The impugned judgment and decrees passed by the appellate court below are hereby set aside and those of the trial court are affirmed.
